newsitem.title: USA: Lightering begins on capsized barge on Mississippi.
newsitem.headline: Lightering begins on capsized barge on Mississippi.

text.p: Crews began lightering a volatile cargo of benzene and gasoline from a capsized barge in the Mississippi River Monday morning, the Coast Guard reported.

The process is expected to be completed by 10 a.m. (CST) Tuesday, Lt. Cheri Ben-Iesau told Reuters. After the barge is emptied, cranes will be used to right it before the river can be fully reopened to marine traffic, she said.
"They pumped in nitrogen to lessen any risk of explosion ad it seems to be going smoothly," she said. "Safety is the number one issue for the whole operation."

The barge capsized March 17 after a tow of 25 barges hit a bridge in the fast-moving, flood-swollen river currents. Several other incidents on the river prompted the Coast Guard to issue restrictions on marine traffic, including a one-way, one vessel or tow at a time limit in the area of the accident.
Two other accidents, one of which involved more than 100 runaway barges, closed the river and snarled vessel movements last week.

No major breakawys were reported during the weekend. "I think with the restrictions, mariners are taking this seriously and finally getting the hang of dealing with this river right now," a Coast Guard spokesman said.
